findings.title: Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called without its UserModel argument
findings.body: `UsernamePasswordForm` only declares `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (UsernamePasswordForm.java:160). A repo-wide grep finds no no-arg overload. `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, so the `services` module does not compile. Either pass `context.getUser()` here, or (preferred, see the other finding) make the helper take no argument.

findings.title: `user != null` in the helper disables passkeys on the initial login form
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` returns false when `user == null`. The old code set up WebAuthn data exactly when the user was NOT yet selected (the removed `context.getUser() == null` check in `challenge(...)` and the `else` branch of `authenticate`). Both call sites now use this helper (lines 115 and 137), so on a normal first-time login (user null) `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm` is never called. The conditional-UI challenge, rpId and `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI` are missing from the page. That breaks auto-login with discoverable keys, the 'username webauthn' autocomplete and the passkey link, which the tests in this PR (e.g. `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey_reauthentication`, `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey`) expect. The same applies to the error re-render in `challenge(context, error, field)` after an invalid username: the passkey form is dropped. The intent of the change is to also cover users already set (re-authentication), so the condition should not depend on the user at all. Drop the parameter: `return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled();`, and update the three call sites (including UsernameForm.java:47).

findings.title: Missing @Override on shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators
findings.body: This method overrides `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` (WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:128) but has no `@Override`. If the superclass signature changes, this override would silently stop applying, and the conditional UI would then show the user's authenticators again.

findings.title: Util class now depends on the browser authenticator package, and a protected constant had to be made public
findings.body: `AuthenticatorUtils` statically imports from `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, which itself imports `AuthenticatorUtils`. That creates a package cycle, and the constant had to be widened from protected to public API. The check duplicates `isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth` (AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.java:257). Consider keeping the helper on `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` as a public static method taking the context, so the constant stays protected.

findings.title: Absence check relies on catching a broad Exception around findElement
findings.body: The block `assertThat(findElement(...), nullValue()); fail(...)` inside `catch (Exception)` passes on any exception, not only `NoSuchElementException`. The sibling test in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest uses `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)`, which is stricter. The same pattern is repeated at line 312.

contracts.action: UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate and challenge(error) set up WebAuthn conditional UI via the new helper isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous code in the same methods filled the WebAuthn context form only when the user was null (the first-login form)
contracts.before_after: Before: fill when passkeys enabled and user is not set. After: fill only when passkeys enabled and user IS set (helper requires user != null). The initial login form therefore no longer gets passkey attributes.
contracts.visible_effect: On a fresh login page the conditional UI, autocomplete 'username webauthn' and the passkey link disappear. They appear only during re-authentication.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent regression of the main passkeys login flow. No error is shown.

contracts.action: UsernameForm.authenticate skips the form during re-authentication unless passkeys are enabled
contracts.equivalent_path: UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate is the superclass path that renders the form when the user is already set
contracts.before_after: The call passes no argument to a method that requires one, so the code does not compile.
contracts.visible_effect: The build of the services module fails.

contracts.action: AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError is now called from badPasswordHandler and from WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse
contracts.equivalent_path: The inline block it replaced in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler, which read the same auth note via isUserAlreadySetBeforeUsernamePasswordAuth
contracts.before_after: The same auth note is read and USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED are set. It is now also applied when a passkey error re-renders the form, so a re-authentication error page keeps the username hidden. The note is set in UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate and removed when user is null.
contracts.visible_effect: After a failed passkey during re-authentication, the form still hides the username field and the registration link.
contracts.failure_mode: None found. In a non-username-password flow the note is absent, so the helper does nothing.

summary: Two blockers in the services code. `UsernameForm.java:47` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no argument, but only a `UserModel` overload exists, so the module does not compile. The helper at `UsernamePasswordForm.java:161` also requires `user != null`, so passkey setup is skipped on the initial login form (user null). It only works during re-authentication, which breaks the main passkeys flow that the new tests expect. The test additions otherwise look consistent: I confirmed `configureTestRealm`, `getInfoMessage` and `getInputError` exist. There are also two minor cleanups (a missing `@Override`, and the package cycle in `AuthenticatorUtils`) and a note on weak absence checks in the tests.
